thread:
jane.d: FYI — canary deploy for svc-auth v2 produced debug logs in the canary environment that include user_id hashes and an Authorization header fragment. Not sure if any full tokens were logged. Sharing a redacted excerpt below, need quick scope + comms guidance.

rob: which cluster and timeframe? can you drop the exact log lines?

jane.d: canary in eu-west-1, around 2026-03-16 21:12 UTC. excerpt (redacted):
```
[DEBUG] 2026-03-16T21:12:07Z svc-auth request id=abc123 user_id_hash=9f3b... status=200 headers={Authorization: "Bearer sk_live_XXx..."}
```

samir: looks like the token was truncated in the log (masked mid-string). hard to tell if full secret ever landed in logs. do we have raw log storage or only streaming through log-provider?

tanya: on the pipeline — canary logs are sent to log-provider with 7d retention; we also forward to hotstore for 24h. need to know whether hotstore contains the raw line or masked.

maria.legal: if any full auth tokens or PII were exposed we need to evaluate notification obligations. for now treat this as potential credential exposure until confirmed. please avoid external comms until legal approves.

infra-bot: Immediate recommended actions:
- stop canary traffic or roll back the deploy
- revoke/rotate any creds possibly affected (short-lived tokens first)
- remove/purge offending lines from hotstore and ask log-provider for expedited deletion from ingestion buffer
- snapshot scope: list of affected request ids, clusters, and time windows

rob: i can kill the canary now and spin up a rollback. jane, can you collect request ids and any user hashes for scoping? samir, can you check hotstore for raw entries?

jane.d: killing canary now. will add request ids to the incident doc.

samir: hotstore shows the same truncated header line for that time window; raw archived bucket (cold) may contain full payloads — permissioned access only. i'll check access logs and report back.

tanya: i'll open a purge request with log-provider and flag it as emergency retention removal. also toggling extra redaction rules for svc-auth.

maria.legal: thanks. draft comms should be internal-first (engineering + support), then customer-facing only if we have confirmed credential exposure and impact. keep statements minimal: what happened, what we know, actions taken, next steps. send draft to me for approval.

jane.d: drafting internal blurb now. question for ops: do we have a short list of customers whose tokens could be affected if tokens were leaked?

rob: only internal service tokens are used in this path for canary; but confirm — if there are any customer tokens we need legal/ps involvement immediately.

samir: checking service token scopes — looks like canary used ephemeral service keys from the rotation pool. still recommend rotating the pool keys and revoking the ones issued in the 21:00–21:20 window.

jane.d: done — incident doc updated with request ids and actions. i've also attached the draft internal blurb in the doc. maria.legal, ping when you can review.

maria.legal: on it. will aim to respond in 30m. do not send anything externally until i confirm.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-0316 created (severity: P2) — responders: eng-oncall, infra, legal.

rob: thanks team. follow-ups: rotate keys, confirm purge, legal sign-off on comms, and a postmortem on how debug-level auth fragments made it into logs. :thumbsup:

jane.d: will keep updates in the incident doc. planning a quick retro/patch PR to add automatic header scrubbing to svc-auth.

samir: once we confirm purge/rotation, i'll run a quick scan for similar patterns across services and share results.

tanya: marking this thread for follow-up in the postmortem channel after legal closes comms.

jane.d: thanks — closing the loop here for now.
